name: Nasal hump reduction

lead: Nasal hump reduction removes or lowers the bony and cartilaginous bump on the bridge of the nose, called the dorsal hump. It is one of the most common techniques in cosmetic rhinoplasty and is used to give the nose a smoother, straighter profile.

Surgeons describe it as a planned step, with osteotomies to close the 'open roof' left after the hump is removed. Newer dorsal preservation approaches aim to lower the hump while keeping the natural dorsum, and randomized trials have compared them with conventional reduction.

paras: A surgeon cuts the cartilage portion of the hump with a scalpel and chisels the bone with an osteotome, then rasps are used to smooth the bone. Osteotomies narrow the bony vault. The nose is taped and splinted, with the dressing removed at about one week and swelling taking a year or more to settle.

A 2022 review says dorsal hump reduction carries a high propensity for aesthetic and functional problems and a nontrivial revision rate. Revision rates of roughly 5 to 20 percent are cited for rhinoplasty in general, with causes including breathing problems and asymmetry. Smoking compromises healing.

chain: Hump on the dorsum is removed or lowered
angle.text: The procedure directly changes the contour of the nasal bridge. People choose it to straighten a profile with a visible bump.

lead: Dorsal hump reduction removes a bump from the bridge of the nose and is one of the most common techniques in modern rhinoplasty [1][2]. It is performed to straighten the nasal profile, usually together with osteotomies to close the open roof left after the hump is removed [1].

In the conventional approach a surgeon cuts the cartilage portion with a scalpel, chisels the bone with an osteotome, then smooths and sculpts the bone with rasps [3]. Ultrasonic (piezoelectric) rhinoplasty, introduced by Massimo Robiony in 2004, offers an alternative way to reshape bone [3]. Jacques Joseph, a Prussian surgeon, described refined nose-reduction techniques through internal incisions in 1928 [3].

Dorsal preservation rhinoplasty is a newer approach that eliminates the hump while preserving the natural dorsal anatomy [4]. Randomized trials have compared preservation and spare-roof techniques with component dorsal hump reduction on functional and aesthetic outcomes [5][6].
Some online communities also discuss do-it-yourself hump filing; this article covers the surgical procedure.
infobox: Scalpel, osteotome, rasp, burr, piezo; dorsal preservation
Splint about one week; swelling may last a year or more
About 5 to 20 percent for rhinoplasty overall

paras: A review of the technique covers planning, instruments, anatomic variables and ways to avoid complications [2]. The hump consists of a bony and a cartilaginous part; component reduction deconstructs and manipulates the parts stepwise to fit anatomy and the desired result [1]. After reduction, osteotomies are used to close the open roof, and they are also indicated for crooked noses and wide bony vaults [7]. Burr-assisted hump reduction and osteoplasty has been studied for effects on hearing in a randomized controlled trial [8].

Dorsal preservation eliminates the hump while keeping the natural dorsal anatomy, using surface manipulation or foundational techniques or both [4]. A randomized prospective study compared dorsal preservation with dorsal hump reduction [5], and another compared the spare roof technique with component reduction in 250 primary rhinoplasties [6].

Hump reduction can disturb the middle vault, and reconstruction of the midvault is described as paramount to good aesthetic and functional outcomes [1]. Spreader grafts address middle vault problems such as internal nasal valve collapse and inverted-V deformity [9]. In East Asian patients, hump reduction is described as an accompanying step to the main goal of augmenting a flattened nose [10].

The nose is typically taped and splinted, with dressing removal at about one week, and swelling can take at least a year to resolve [3]. Revision rhinoplasty is needed in roughly 5 to 20 percent of operations, for reasons including breathing problems, asymmetry and a scooped nose [3]. Smoking compromises healing [3]. A randomized trial studied tranexamic acid for rhinoplasty side effects [11].

Randomized and prospective studies include a trial of dorsal preservation versus dorsal hump reduction [5], a 250-patient randomized study of the spare roof technique versus component reduction [6], a randomized study of burr-assisted rhinoplasty and hearing [8], a 200-patient study of cartilage gel versus diced cartilage for dorsal camouflage after reduction [12], and a randomized study of tranexamic acid [11]. Reviews cover osteotomies [7], hump reduction [2][1] and dorsal preservation experience [4].

timeline.event: Jacques Joseph publishes a text on refined nose-reduction rhinoplasty through internal incisions [3].
